samples.summary: No test covers the cross-tab chart/pivot range pass that the new endpoints advertise
samples.evidence: The controller docstring (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:37-41) explicitly claims the row/column endpoints include "the cross-tab pass that repoints other tabs' chart ranges at the edited one", and both `applyShift` (line 193) and `moveAxis` (line 155) call `shiftCrossTabDataRanges` / `moveCrossTabDataRanges`. The new controller spec seeds only the single default tab `tab-1` (worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts:12, seed/read helpers) and never creates a second tab with a chart or `pivotTable.sourceTabId`, so nothing asserts a cross-tab range is repointed. A repo-wide grep for `CrossTabDataRanges` finds only the definitions in packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:425,454, the index re-exports, and the two call sites — no test file at all. If these functions mis-shift a source range, charts/pivots on other tabs silently point at the wrong data and no suite would fail.

samples.summary: Newly extracted `normalizeStoredCell` has no direct test; spill-field preservation is untested after the extraction
samples.evidence: `normalizeStoredCell` is a new export (worksheet-grid.ts:238) that replaces YorkieStore.normalizeCell (yorkie-store.ts:215) and is now the normalizer used by the backend structural endpoints. Grep for `normalizeStoredCell` returns only worksheet-grid.ts, index.ts, yorkie-store.ts and the backend controller — no test. The moved sheets suite still defines its own local `normalizeCell` (packages/sheets/test/workbook/worksheet-structure.test.ts:14-28) that handles only v/f/s, so it does not exercise the shared function, and neither it nor any frontend test asserts the spillAnchor/spillRows/spillCols/spillBlocked pass-through or the null-for-empty-cell return. A regression there (e.g. dropping spill metadata during a row insert) would silently corrupt spilled ranges with a green suite.

samples.summary: The upper bounds on `count` (and on a row `index`) — the stated DoS guard — are never tested
samples.evidence: `parseCount` rejects `count > axisLimit(axis)` (worksheet-structure.ts:143-156) and the comment justifies it as the analogue of the clear-range area cap, i.e. a resource guard. The new spec only tests count 0, missing count, and fractional/zero index (worksheet-structure-axis.spec.ts:30-40); the bound test at :43-51 checks the *index* limit for a column only. Nothing asserts `{axis:'row', count: 2_000_000}` or `{axis:'row', index: 2_000_000}` is rejected, so silently weakening or removing that guard would not fail the suite.

samples.summary: No test that a structural edit against an unknown tabId raises NotFoundException
samples.evidence: `worksheetOrThrow` (controller line 64-71) throws NotFoundException when `root.sheets[tabId]` is missing, and it is now reached from three new endpoints inside `doc.update`. The new controller spec always uses the existing `tab-1` (worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts:13) and only covers the BadRequest paths (invalid body, non-sheet document). Nothing asserts the missing-tab behaviour, and because the throw happens inside `doc.update` the surfaced error/rollback behaviour is exactly the part most likely to regress unnoticed.

samples.summary: Validation-before-open and non-sheet-document guards are only asserted for `insertAxis`
samples.evidence: The 'rejects an invalid request' test exercises insertAxis and moveAxis (lines 146-160) and the non-sheet test only insertAxis (lines 163-172); `deleteAxis`'s guard ordering (assertSheetDocument then parseAxisShift then negate) is never checked, so e.g. a delete that opened the document before validating would pass.
